To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two newly identified ω-TAs, cloned with a Strep-tag II or His6-tag, were employed for the enantioselective synthesis of a variety of amines with high conversion (>99 %) and enantioselectivity (>99 %).

two new (S)-selectivew-ω-transaminases were identified, cloned, and expressed in Escherichia coli and that the His-tagged recombi- nant transaminase showed significantly higher stereoselection than the corresponding commercial enzyme prepa- ration.

the two new ω-TAs, Strep-PD-omegaTA and PF-omegaTA, are highly efficient biocatalysts for the synthesis of chiral amines, and that the His-tagged recomminant ωTA from Vibrio Fluvialis (His‐VF‐omegaTA) is a more efficient catalyst for the amination of ethyl acetoate than the commercial preparation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and optimization of two new ω-TAs for the synthesis of chiral amines and the His-tagged ω-aminotransferase from V. fluvialis, which is a novel ω-aminotranferase with high stereoselectivity.
the development of a novel biocatalytic process for the asymmetric aminations of selected prochirals.
the identification and application of novel (S)-selectively active ω-TAs for the synthesis of optically pure a-aminoketones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two new (S)-selectivities ω-TAs are highly promising biocatalysts for the amination of a broad range of ketone substrates.
the two new ω-TAs, Strep-PD-omega-ωTA and PF-ωTA, are promising biocatalysts for the synthesis of enantiomerically pure aminotransferase products.
all three ω-TAs tested in this study showed excellent stereoselectivity, and the His-tagged ω-TAs showed high conversion rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Strep-PD-omega TA is a very useful enzyme for amination of ketones with a wide variety of substrates.
the new ω-TAs are promising tools for the asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines, and that the His-tag can improve the stereoselectivity of ω-TAs.
the Strep-PD-omegaTA, PF-omegaTA and His-VF-omegaTA are promising biocatalysts for the amination of prochiral ketone substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the two new ω-TAs, Strep-PD- and PF-ωTA, are highly efficient biocatalysts for the asymmetric aminations of prochiral ketone derivatives and the His-tagged ω- transaminase from V. fluvialis, His-VF-ω- TA, shows significantly higher stereoselection for the amination of ethyl aceto acetate than the corresponding commercial enzyme.
the newly cloned ω-TAs are promising biocatalysts for the asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines.

(i) the Strep-tagged ω-TAs are highly efficient biocatalysts for the asymmetric aminations of selected prochirally substituted ketones and (ii) that the His-tagged VF-ωTA is a highly efficient biocata-lyst for asymmetric amination reactions, which could also be used in the synthesis of chiral amines.
